structs.description: One step of what a task did, in the order it did it (decision 0148). A closed kind, an optional host, a count and a time; never page text, model text, a tool name, or an address beyond the host.

fields.name: host
fields.description: The host it happened to, where the kind is about a page, bounded by MAX_SOURCE_HOST_BYTES. A host and never a full address: the host is what the sentence needs, and a path is where a query string and a session token live. Absent where the kind is not about a page, and absent rather than guessed where the task knows no consented source for the tab.

fields.name: count
fields.description: How many, where the kind counts something — the facts an output was built from. Nought where the kind counts nothing, which includes READ_PAGE: what a read found is a number of facts, and facts belong to the workspace rather than to the task, so a surface joins the host to its own source list for that number.

fields.name: at_epoch_ms

The millisecond lives inside rather than beside it because a timestamp with no refusal has no honest value, and a zero would read as the start of the process.

fields.name: refusal

fields.name: at_monotonic_ms

Every field is optional because the catalog may say nothing, and a surface that is told nothing shows nothing rather than a placeholder. Prose — what to try when a key is refused, how a vendor words its own plans — is deliberately absent: that is written in the product's own strings, in the person's own language, and is never served.

fields.name: key_prefix
fields.description: What this vendor's keys begin with, for a form that wants to say 'that does not look like one of these' before spending a call proving it.

fields.name: get_key_url

fields.name: docs_url
fields.description: Where the vendor documents this endpoint. https only.

fields.name: provider_id
fields.description: The provider this model belongs to, matching a roster row.

fields.name: model_id

fields.name: display_name
fields.description: The name to show.

fields.name: roles
fields.description: What the catalog cataloged this model for, in catalog order.

fields.name: input_modalities
fields.description: What the model accepts.

fields.name: thinking_levels

structs.name: ProviderRosterEntry
structs.description: One provider as a surface should draw it: identity, offered methods, and the stored credential's registry facts. Projected from the core's provider plane; the browser secure store is the other half of 'connected', which a surface intersects rather than trusts alone.

fields.name: provider_id
fields.description: Stable identity, and the key any credential is filed under.

fields.name: display_name
fields.description: The name to show.

fields.name: origin
fields.description: Catalog or the person's own.

fields.name: auth_methods
fields.description: Every method this provider offers, in catalog order. A person's own provider offers API_KEY.

fields.name: stored
fields.description: The stored credential's registry facts, absent when nothing is stored.

fields.name: signing_in
fields.description: Whether a sign-in flow is currently admitted and pending for this provider.

fields.name: enabled
fields.description: The catalog kill switch. A disabled provider is still listed so a surface can say it was switched off rather than hiding it.

fields.name: endpoint_host
fields.description: The endpoint's host, for a person's own provider only. Never a path or a query.

fields.name: configurable
fields.description: Whether this build can act on the row: at least one declared method has a working entry path in this binary. A served row must not claim what the binary cannot do, so an unconfigurable provider is listed and explained rather than offered.

fields.name: endpoint_changed
fields.description: The served catalog asked to move this provider’s endpoint host and the endpoint guard refused. The surface states it and pauses key entry; nothing ever connects to the refused host.

fields.name: catalog_layer
fields.description: Which layer supplied this row.

fields.name: selected_model_id
fields.description: The model this person pinned for this provider, absent while the provider's own order stands. Always a model the catalog still carries: a pin whose model leaves the catalog is dropped rather than shown against nothing.

fields.name: thinking
fields.description: How much thinking this person asked this provider for, absent while Taffy decides.

fields.name: presentation
fields.description: The catalog's few behavioural facts for a setup surface, absent when the catalog said none.

fields.name: endpoint_base
fields.description: The whole base address of a person's own provider, bounded by MAX_PROVIDER_ENDPOINT_BYTES, absent for a catalog row. A new field rather than a widening of endpoint_host, which exists to be shown in disclosure text and promises no path and no port; a person's address carries both, and an edit screen that cannot prefill what they typed makes them type it again.

fields.name: last_refusal
fields.description: The last refusal this provider answered with while its credential was usable, absent when there has been none. The composer's quota banner has no other signal: ProviderCredentialStateView is about the key and every one of its members says the key is the subject.

fields.name: model_count
fields.description: How many models this provider carries in the merged catalog, before CoreStatus.provider_models was fitted to MAX_PROVIDER_MODEL_ENTRIES. It sits beside the flat list rather than being derived from it: the list is what survived the shared budget, and counting a provider's rows in it is the silent truncation decisions 0096 section 5 and 0098 section 4 both refuse.

fields.name: subscription
fields.description: Whether OAUTH on this row means a plan the person already pays for, as the catalog states it. Not derivable from auth_methods, and that is the whole reason it crosses: an OAUTH exchange that mints a metered API key is spent exactly as a pasted one is, so calling it a subscription would put a plan sentence in front of somebody billed by the token. The catalog already draws the line (openrouter carries false and says why in its provenance); a surface that grouped by auth_methods alone could not, and filed a metered vendor under a tab named for plans.

fields.name: refused_endpoint_host
fields.description: The host the served document asked this provider's compiled address to move to and the browser refused (decision 0080), bounded by MAX_SOURCE_HOST_BYTES. Present only while the refusal stands, so it is exactly as present as endpoint_changed is true; absent otherwise. Disclosure only: a surface may name the host it did not connect to, and nothing ever connects to it. A host rather than an address for the same reason endpoint_host is one — this exists to be shown, never dialled.

fields.name: provider_id

fields.name: verdict
fields.description: What the one bounded call proved.

fields.name: at_monotonic_ms
fields.description: When the verdict was reached, browser monotonic milliseconds, so a surface can say how stale it is.

fields.name: endpoint

structs.name: ProbeEndpointView
structs.description: What one endpoint probe read from the server's own answer, so a surface can say what it found instead of asking a person to confirm what they typed.

fields.name: server_kind
fields.description: The runtime the server identified itself as.

fields.name: model_count
fields.description: How many models it named. Zero is an answer: the address is right and there is nothing loaded behind it.

fields.name: models
fields.description: The models that survived the bound of MAX_CUSTOM_MODEL_ENTRIES, in the order the server listed them. Beside model_count rather than instead of it: the count is what the server named and this is what fitted, and collapsing the two is the silent truncation decisions 0096 section 5 and 0098 section 4 both refuse.

fields.description: The base the OpenAI-shaped API actually answered at, bounded by MAX_PROVIDER_ENDPOINT_BYTES, absent when nothing was proved. The transport joins only the operation beneath a person's base, so http://box:11434/v1 routes and a bare http://box:11434 routes to /chat/completions, which no runtime serves - while a native probe step succeeds on that bare origin. This is which of the two the prober proved, so a save is filed against an address that works.

structs.name: DetectedServerView
structs.description: One runtime name, wrapped so it can be absent. A record rather than a member meaning 'no member', for the same reason ThinkingPreferenceView is one: the interface projects to mojom, which has no optional enumeration, and 'nothing was detected' must not be spelled as a detection.

fields.name: server_kind
fields.description: The runtime the probe read from the server's own answer.

fields.name: site

fields.name: username
fields.description: Sensitive display metadata. It may be drawn on this screen and must never be logged, journalled, or sent to a model.

fields.name: last_used_epoch_ms
